newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-American Intn'l Q2 oper shr up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-American Intn'l Q2 oper shr up.

text.p: American International Group Inc. on Thursday reported better-than-expected second quarter profits, boosted by strong results in financial services and solid performances in its other businesses.
American International said second quarter operating earnings rose to $811.4 million, or $1.73 a share pre-split, compared with $712.6 million, or $1.51 a share a year ago.
The First Call consensus estimate was for $1.69 a share.
The New York-based insurer's financial services business turned in very strong results, with pre-tax operating income up 30.8 percent in the second quarter to $173.6 million.
Premium income in AIG's large worldwide life insurance business rose 17.5 percent in the second quarter before the impact of foreign exchange.
In its core worldwide property-casualty business, net premiums written grew 7.5 percent in the second quarter before the impact of foreign exchange.

The property-casualty premium growth fell slightly short of Wall Street's expectations, but that was more than offset by the strength of AIG's life insurance and financial services businesses, analysts said.
"People tend to focus on the premium growth within general insurance," Merrill Lynch analyst Jay Cohen said. "It was OK, but I don't think there was any big surprise in the number," he said.
In the United States, AIG said property-casualty net premiums rose more than 10 percent, exclusive of the risk management business, in a very competitive marketplace.
Workers' compensation rates, in particular, continued to fall to unacceptable levels in a number of states, AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said in a statement.
But, "domestic personal lines had a very good quarter, with continued growth in net premiums written," he said.
"Our direct auto business in the United States is showing strong growth and excellent results," he said.
In the foreign property-casualty business, net premiums written rose 5.1 percent, pressured by tough conditions in the London market and economic conditions in Thailand, AIG said.
Weakness in the Japanese economy also contributed, Merrill's Cohen said.
The life insurance business, however, turned in another strong quarter, anaylsts said.
AIG's worldwide life insurance operations reported second quarter 1997 pretax income before realized capital gains of $389.0 million, an increase of 20.1 percent, compared to $323.9 million in 1996.

"The life insurance operations are starting to pick up some speed and probably will offset any slowdown (in growth) in the property-casualty operations," Salomon analyst Michael Smith said. "This is what a good insurance operation is all about," he said.
"The surprise was in the relatively more volatile financial services area," he said.
AIG continued its program to repurchase shares of its common stock in the open market. For the six months ended June 30, AIG said, it repurchased approximately 2.3 million shares.
AIG shares rose $3.625, or more than two percent, to close at $156.50 on the the New York Stock Exchange.
